source-level same-family comparison (rest face vs grpc face): lib/api/src/grpc/qdrant.rs CreateCollection.shard_number has #[validate(range(min = 1))] with NO max (line 1186-1188) — both interface faces share the identical unbounded domain; contrast lib/api/src/rest/schema.rs:751 #[validate(range(max = 16_384))] // artificial maximum, to avoid too expensive query. and VectorParams.size capped 65536 on both faces — the codebase's deliberate artificial-maximum pattern was applied to sibling resource fields but not to shard_number

http_semantics.note: The killing request is spec-legal (constraint premise: >=1, uint32, no documented max), so the 2xx/4xx business-code question does not apply to it; the server returned NO HTTP response at all (connection aborted mid-request) and then /healthz died — the forbidden 'crash the service' outcome itself. For contrast, the genuinely client-erroneous neighbors in the same log were correctly returned as HTTP 422 (shard_number=0) and HTTP 400 (shard_number=-1).

contract_grounding.note: Observed value 4294967295 is inside the quote's constraint domain (>= 1, uint32, no documented max per the v1.18.x spec shard), so violates=true is a genuine domain violation: none of the three permitted dispositions occurred — not completed (no 2xx), not rejected with an error (no 4xx at all; connection aborted with no response), not a documented service error (no 5xx body; process died, /healthz unreachable x3). source_grounding.call_chain_traced: PUT /collections/{name} -> CreateCollection request struct (collection_meta_ops.rs: #[validate(range(min = 1))] Option<u32>, NO max — this validator is what returned the observed 422 for shard_number=0; serde u32 rejected -1 with 400) -> toc create_collection.rs (only NonZeroU32 zero-guard at line 135; debug_assert-only consistency vs distribution) -> toc/mod.rs suggest_shard_distribution (user value passed through NonZeroU32::new) -> shard_distribution.rs ShardDistributionProposal::new line 91: (0..shard_number.get()).map(...).collect() — with shard_number=4294967295 this eagerly materializes a Vec of 4,294,967,295 (ShardId, Vec<PeerId>) entries, each replica-Vec its own heap allocation, before any shard object exists -> allocation exhaustion kills the process (observed as RemoteDisconnected mid-request + connection-refused /healthz x3). No upper-bound, resource, or pre-flight feasibility check exists anywhere on this path; callers do not re-validate. Searched whole tree for shard upper-bound guards: none for shard_number (only VectorParams.size 65536 both faces, candidates_limit 16384 with explicit 'artificial maximum' comment, grpc misc caps).

mundane_explanation.surviving: Resource-exhaustion process death eagerly triggered by a spec-legal shard_number: the unguarded (0..shard_number.get()) materialization in ShardDistributionProposal::new (and the per-shard object creation it feeds) exhausts memory within ~3s of the request; the exact terminal mechanism (allocator abort vs OS OOM-kill vs panic) is not distinguishable from client-side evidence alone, but every variant is the 'crash the service' outcome the constraint forbids. Note the graded escalation in the same log — 1000 and 100000 timed out client-side yet left /healthz alive, only uint32-max killed it — consistent with a resource threshold, not a logic error.
